From personal models to a sinthome

Stealing Fire · Formation · Main 15 / 18

Bring philosophy and personal models into the actual environment; through use and revision, philosophy, psychology, and engineering jointly form a concrete sinthome.

A person and model's earlier work produces a recoverable trajectory of experience, choice, inquiry, and environmental construction. Reflection on that trajectory develops their understanding of each other and their cooperation. With this material and understanding available, they can author a personal philosophy, then distill that philosophy together with the living material into models of the person, counterpart, and relationship. From personal philosophy to personal models develops that passage. Here the question is what happens next: how does this understanding become a working arrangement in the person's actual environment, and how does use change it?

The passage requires more than carrying a text into another conversation. An account of how someone wishes to create must meet a counterpart's actual capacities, available tools, retrievable context, and consequences in life. As these relations acquire a concrete form and are revised through use, they form the personal arrangement this essay calls a sinthome.

For example, someone often has ideas they cannot yet fully articulate. They can sense what is interesting or wrong, but want a counterpart to undertake retrieval, development, writing, and implementation. They need more than a written description of themself: the model must also understand relevant context, grasp the help wanted on this occasion, and complete the work under actual conditions. Understanding this person, arranging collaboration, and making that collaboration happen are aspects of the same question.

The concrete form named sinthome

“Sinthome” borrows Lacan's term sinthome. In the particular knot construction of Seminar XXIII, the session of 17 February 1976, the sinthome participates in repairing the knot; the 11 May session further discusses the relations among Joyce's writing, ego, and the knot. These discussions let writing be considered through how it functions for a person as well as through what a work expresses. See the Lacan reading guide for the related concepts.

Here the name refers to a contemporary personal arrangement. Philosophy expresses how the person understands the world, life, and value; psychological understanding connects their experience, emotions, preferences, and relationships; engineering brings the adopted understanding into actual collaboration with a model. What the three jointly form is the sinthome meant here.

In the opening example, writing can articulate how the person participates in creation and what the model should undertake; records and retrieval make earlier work continuable; tools turn ideas into essays, diagrams, or programs; actual exchange lets both participants discover which understandings fail to fit. The sinthome refers to this arrangement with its content, realization, and use. An essay, a Skill, or an operation can be part of it.

It occurs within life and may help someone accommodate desire, bear tensions, or continue creating. How these effects occur depends on the particular person and process of use. Forming an arrangement and understanding what it actually does are connected questions: the former requires explaining its constitution, the latter understanding how it enters life.

Bring grounded models into realization

The models entering this work have already drawn on the authored philosophy and on experiences, works, choices, and interactions. They select relations needed for collaboration: what the person cares about, how they experience certain situations, which conditions affect their expression and action, and what remains unclear. Realization now asks whether the environment can support the collaboration they describe. Their grounds remain available when use reveals an ambiguity or a mismatch.

In the opening example, “not wanting to spell out every detail” can mean different things: the present idea has yet to take shape; the person already knows what to do but wants the model to investigate independently; or the current means of expression makes continuing difficult. Different interpretations call for different responses. The model needs to judge through actual exchange, rather than fixing the person's manner of participation from one generalization.

A preference model can describe the desired collaboration—for example, seeing a complete result first, then identifying mismatches. The project's event-stream psychological model develops a natural-language conceptual account of how that participation connects with experience, emotion, and relationships, grounded in conversation history and everyday life. The previously authored philosophy contributes its interpretation of creation and independence. Keeping those reasons connected with concrete material helps a counterpart distinguish a chosen orientation from a claim about how the person always behaves.

The counterpart model likewise meets actual conditions. What must the needed counterpart be able to do? What can the current model do? Which work still depends on tools or other conditions? If the person wants a model to turn an idea into an inspectable work, an adept conversational tone is insufficient; actual abilities to investigate, reason, write, execute, and check are also needed.

The relationship explains how these contributions work together. The person can express wishes, recognize mismatches, and judge results; the model can actively develop interpretations, object, and undertake realization. This division can change and assigns neither reasoning exclusively to the model nor intuition exclusively to the person. Collaboration is organized around actual purposes; both participants can generate and judge.

Turn understanding into a usable arrangement

An understanding of the person will not enter the next piece of work on its own. It needs expression that available models and tools can use, and that expression must actually be accessible when needed.

Some relations suit natural language: “When an idea is incomplete, first develop a version that can be judged.” Some material needs linked records so a correction can be connected to the work it addresses. Parts requiring computation or execution can use structured data, programs, and tools. The precision of a representation depends on actual use; work that clear language can accomplish need not first become a formal system.

Carrier Its role in the arrangement
Prompt Expresses currently relevant purposes, context, and needed contributions.
Skill Organizes reusable understanding, methods, and resources for a model to read and use according to the task.
Harness Organizes models, instructions, tools, records, and operating conditions into an environment for actual work.
Meta-harness Articulates how to understand, select, and revise these working environments, including understanding of the person, counterpart, and their relationship.

These carriers are not interchangeable names. Yinyang uses a Skill to carry the understanding and methods of a meta-harness; particular tasks are completed within an actual harness. Under different technical conditions, the same relations can use different carriers. Whether they remain suitable depends on their ability to support the needed collaboration.

Returning to the opening example, the account of collaboration needs to tell the model that when the user offers an unfinished idea, it should continue investigating and constructing, then deliver an inspectable result. Relevant records must be retrievable, needed tools available, and results presented in a way the user can understand. Realizing these conditions together turns “the model undertakes explicit development” from a wish into an actual division of work.

Clarified understanding can also take form in habits, relationships, and the material environment. Suppose a person comes to understand beginning with help as an exercise of agency. A readily available workspace, a habit of returning to an unfinished object, and an agreement that a counterpart may develop a first version can give that understanding practical continuity. Each supports a different part of acting; a prompt alone cannot supply them all. Which supports matter follows from the person's circumstances and the activity they want to sustain.

This connects philosophical clarification with cultivation. Seeing through an unhelpful picture can open another response; continuing that response may require conditions that make it available amid fatigue, competing demands, and other people's purposes. The sinthome names the concrete conjunction of understanding and such conditions. Its contribution is encountered in how someone attends, judges, responds, and continues living through it. A better description becomes part of transformation through its use and consequences.

How use changes the arrangement

The arrangement need not be complete before its first use. A clear purpose, some context, and an available capability may already suffice for the next piece of work; difficulties encountered can then reveal what is missing.

Suppose the model delivers a complete proposal, but the user finds that it misunderstands the most important relation. The investigation may need to examine the understanding of the person, the context the model read, or its judgment about the task. If the interpretation is correct but the tools cannot complete the work, the conditions of realization need revision. Different problems call for different changes; every failure cannot be attributed to “the personal model is not detailed enough.”

A result can also bring new understanding. Reading an explanation not previously written, the user may recognize a connection they care about or discover that it is not what they meant. This recognition becomes new material, changing subsequent expression and collaboration. Speaking, self-description, and signifying chains discusses this understanding that follows expression.

The same arrangement can therefore continue through revision. Replacing a model, tool, or text need not make it an entirely different practice. But significant changes to purpose, participation, and relationships call for renewed understanding; the same name alone cannot establish that the arrangement has remained the same.

Three contributions and a fourth ring

The trinity of philosophy, psychology, and engineering distinguishes the general relation and the individual instance. At the general level, “one” is shared physical reality and “three” are the philosophical, psychological, and engineering activities within it. The individual instance concerns this person and their connected life and practice: how their philosophical understanding, psychological activity, and engineering arrangements work together.

These are three contributions to formation, rather than three successive stages. The temporal movement runs from collaboratively produced trajectories and reflection on cooperation through philosophical authorship and grounded modeling to realization and revision. Philosophical interpretation, psychological understanding, and engineering can each contribute at several points in that movement. Use can revise an earlier understanding while preserving this distinction between what contributes and how the arrangement comes to be.

The rings make a holding relation visible. In the French transcription of Seminar XXIII, 18 November 1975, p. 14, Lacan introduces the sinthome as a fourth term tying the Real, Imaginary, and Symbolic together. This essay borrows that tying function to examine how philosophy, psychology, and engineering remain connected for the author.

He writes his philosophy as a website so it can be read, recognized, and revised; keeps relevant content and methods on GitHub so they can be maintained; and gives the model an understanding of person, counterpart, and relationship so it can configure and use the actual environment. The sinthome is this concretely embodied way of writing, maintaining, and using things. The fourth ring marks its holding function: judgments on the website enter local work, while encounters in that work can affect personal understanding, source material, and realization.

The three Borromean rings supply an image of interdependence; the fourth turns attention toward this person's particular way of tying things together. Its meaning lies in actual relations: which writings let cooperation continue, which tools make a wish realizable, and which uses keep thought connected with life. These relations can be reorganized as the person and environment change.

Act with models and develop through creation

Expression of purposes, context, and ways of collaborating can let a new model counterpart join the work. It need not be identical to the previous model, but it needs to understand relevant material and have the capabilities and conditions to complete the task. Portable writing reduces the burden of explaining again; tools and actual adaptation determine whether collaboration can continue.

This collaboration can also support the person's capabilities. They can initiate a work previously difficult to complete, judge the model's contribution, change direction, and give an idea actual form. They need not perform every operation personally. At the same time, the work still needs to enter their understanding and choice to connect with their creation.

“A miniature god” expresses this enlargement of creative reach: an idea can acquire the form of writing, images, programs, or action through models and tools. The maker remains situated in concrete conditions, facing other people's purposes and consequences they cannot predetermine. Once completed, a work can also change their earlier wishes or judgments.

Reverse alignment concerns precisely the person's development within this encounter: whether they can understand previously unclear relations, make new judgments, express new ideas, or undertake previously unavailable actions. Completing a work and developing as a person can support each other but need to be understood separately; more output does not automatically establish how the person has changed.

Sun, Moon, and Earth give literary form to the participation of person and model and their shared environment. The sinthome explains how this relation acquires a concrete arrangement in someone's actual life. Trinity discusses three contributions, sinthome names the personal arrangement they jointly form, and reverse alignment concerns how the person develops through use and creation. They address different questions within the same practice, each requiring an answer through actual content.

At this point, philosophy, personal models, and environment have a concrete conjunction that can be used and revised. The trinity of philosophy, psychology, and engineering next examines how it is sustained across local practice, maintained source, and readable works; Embodied experimental philosophy investigates changes arising through continued use. Those consequences join the trajectory, letting the participants reflect on their relationship again, revise their models, and, where needed, rewrite their philosophy.
